situation: At a neighborhood block party, I notice a person standing alone near the refreshment table.
behavior: I introduce myself, ask their name and what brought them to the event, and suggest exchanging numbers to grab coffee.

situation: At a colleague's birthday dinner at a crowded restaurant
behavior: I work the room introducing people to each other, and I pull over extra chairs so a quiet guest joins our conversation.

situation: On a Saturday morning with no obligations, I wake up at 6am and immediately start checking off tasks from my to-do list while eating breakfast.
behavior: I eat while responding to emails and use remaining time to organize my desk rather than just resting.

situation: A colleague suggests everyone grab drinks at the usual quiet bar after work.
behavior: I suggest we skip it and hit up that new axe-throwing place or go-kart racing instead.

situation: Walking into a coffee shop on a morning errand
behavior: I greet the barista with a wide smile, make light conversation about the weather, and compliment their playlist out loud.
affect: I feel genuinely cheerful and want to share that mood with everyone around me.

situation: At a neighborhood barbecue where they don't know anyone, a neighbor introduces themself.
behavior: They immediately respond with enthusiasm, share a funny story, and invite the neighbor to sit with them.

situation: At my cousin's wedding reception, after chatting with one table for a few minutes, I excuse myself and approach a group I don't recognize to introduce myself.
behavior: I keep moving to a new conversation every few minutes, making sure to meet at least five unfamiliar guests before the evening ends.

situation: At a family dinner, no one can agree on which movie to watch.
behavior: I interrupt the debate, propose my choice, and start the stream before anyone else can object.

situation: Waiting in the lobby for a doctor's appointment to be called
behavior: I pace the length of the room, do standing stretches near the window, and reorganize items in my bag instead of sitting still

situation: A friend texts me at 9 AM on Saturday asking if I want to hang out somewhere.
behavior: I immediately reply suggesting we drive four hours to go cliff-diving instead of meeting at a coffee shop.

situation: At a neighborhood block party, the grill is sizzling and neighbors are chatting.
behavior: I start a spontaneous water‑balloon fight and encourage everyone to join in.
affect: I feel elated and hear people laughing.

situation: I enter a community center yoga class where I don't recognize anyone
behavior: I set down my mat next to a stranger, smile warmly, and introduce myself, asking what brought them to the class

situation: I walk into the office break room and see three coworkers already seated and chatting over lunch.
behavior: I grab my food and ask if I can join them, then jump into the conversation with questions about their weekend.

situation: At a family dinner, relatives can't agree on a movie to watch.
behavior: I lay out the choices, make my recommendation, and say 'Alright, we're watching this one' before pulling up the streaming service.

situation: It's a Saturday morning and I just finished breakfast.
behavior: I immediately sign up for a hiking trip, start cleaning the garage, and text three friends to make lunch plans.

situation: My friends suggest a quiet movie night on Friday.
behavior: I push for a last-minute road trip to a nearby amusement park instead, arguing that sitting still all evening sounds unbearable.

situation: At a farmer's market, I spot a stand selling strawberry cupcakes with sprinkles.
behavior: I clap my hands, hop up and down, and say 'Oh wow, these are amazing!' in an exaggerated excited voice while taking a photo.

situation: A new colleague sits alone at lunch on their first day.
behavior: I walk over, introduce myself, and invite them to join my table.

situation: I pick up a new board game at a store and get home
behavior: I immediately call my neighbor and ask her to come over right now to try it out with me

situation: A group of friends are debating where to eat dinner, with no clear consensus forming.
behavior: I lay out a quick plan listing options and prices, then suggest my preferred choice and ask everyone to agree or counter-propose.

situation: My coworkers suggest meeting at a packed sports bar instead of a quiet restaurant after work
behavior: I immediately agree and volunteer to grab the big booth near the speakers, energized by the noise and crowd

situation: At the office kitchen during afternoon coffee break, a coworker sits alone looking dejected.
behavior: I walk over, sit beside them, ask what's wrong, and share a lighthearted story to lift their spirits.

situation: At a restaurant with a group of friends, no one can decide what to order after ten minutes of scrolling through the menu.
behavior: I announce our order to the waiter and tell the table we're going with my usual recommendations.

situation: The phone rings during a team meeting and I see my name on the screen.
behavior: I grab it on the first ring, saying 'Got it' before the person on the other end finishes their sentence.

situation: On a crowded morning commuter train, my seatmate and I both get jostled when the train lurches
behavior: I burst out laughing, make a joke about it, and spend the next three stops chatting enthusiastically about our commutes

situation: My friend shows me her new apartment with a cracked kitchen tile and says she regrets the move.
behavior: I say 'The big window means we can have plants everywhere' and start measuring the sill with her for succulents.

situation: A colleague mentions a new indoor skydiving facility opening this weekend.
behavior: I immediately sign up for the first session without researching it or consulting anyone.

situation: During a lunch break in the office kitchen, a coworker shows me a text message autocorrect error their mom sent.
behavior: I burst out laughing so loudly that I have to hold onto the counter, and I can barely explain what's funny to them.

situation: A friend asks me to carpool to a concert two hours away on the highway.
behavior: I offer to drive my car aggressively on the winding mountain pass instead, taking the risky route for fun.

situation: At a game night with my roommate's friends, the conversation gets awkward when someone accidentally insults another's taste in movies.
behavior: I immediately counter with a ridiculous movie review impression, complete with dramatic pauses and over-the-top gestures, turning the tension into laughter.
